The company has lighting and electrical consumer durables including LED lighting, fans, pumps, and household appliances like water heaters, air coolers, and kitchen appliances.{{Cite web |last=Debangana |first=Ghosh |date=2020-09-05 |title=Crompton Greaves Consumer Electricals has been doing well but there is a tightrope walk ahead |url=https://www.outlookbusiness.com/markets/feature/crompton-greaves-consumer-electricals-has-been-doing-well-but-there-is-a-tightrope-walk-ahead-5981 |access-date=2022-03-07 |website=[[Outlook (Indian magazine)|Outlook Business]]}}{{Cite web |last=Praveen |first=Sahay |title=Crompton Greaves Consumer Electricals Ltd: Q2FY17 Result Update |url=https://www.edelweiss.in/ewwebimages/WebFiles/Research/2f7d582f-08ab-444e-a19c-dbe66e5f217b.pdf |access-date=2022-03-07 |website=Edelweiss}} == History == The company was established in 1937 as Crompton Parkinson Works Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary of [[Crompton Parkinson]]. In 1947, it was acquired by [[Karam Chand Thapar]].{{Cite web |last=Zaveri |first=Jimit |date=2020-09-30 |title=Initiating Coverage Crompton Greaves Consumer Electricals Limited |url=https://www.hdfcsec.com/hsl.research.pdf/Initiating%20Coverage%20-%20Crompton%20Greaves%20Consumer%20Electricals%20Ltd%20-%20300920.pdf |access-date=2022-03-07 |website=[[HDFC securities]]}}{{Cite thesis |last=Seth |first=Amit |date=2010|title=A Study of Turnaround Strategies of Indian Corporate Sector - An Analysis of Selected Companies |url=https://core.ac.uk/download/pdf/144527033.pdf |type=PhD Thesis |publisher=Aligarh Muslim University|pages=105|via=[[CORE (research service)]]}} The company was established in 2016 as an outcome of the demerger of Crompton Greaves Limited which separated the latter's consumer goods business from the power and industrial systems segment.{{Cite SSRN|last=Bhattacharyya |first=Asish K. |date=2020-12-12 |title=Evolution of Corporate Governance in Emerging Economies – Indian Experience |language=en |ssrn=3747512 }} The demerger plan was announced in July 2014 and it was completed in 2016 with the creation of [[CG Power and Industrial Solutions]] and Crompton Greaves Consumer Electricals Limited.{{Cite web |last=Jayaprakash |first=Rinu |date=October 2017 |title=AN ANALYSIS OF THE PERFORMANCE OF NIFTY INFRASTRUCTURE INDEX STOCKS |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/347509026 |access-date=2022-03-07 |website=Journal of Arts, Science & Commerce |issn=2231-4172}}{{Cite journal |last1=Bose |first1=Indranil |last2=Lahiri |first2=Saikat |date=2020 |title=Crompton: Innovation in Anti-Dust Fans |url=https://www.iimcal.ac.in/sites/all/files/case_studies_portal/crompton_sneak_peek.pdf |journal=IIM Calcutta Case Research Center |via=[[Indian Institute of Management Calcutta]]}} At the time of demerger, [[Gautam Thapar]], the former chairman of combined Crompton Greaves Limited, sold his 34% stake in CGCEL to [[Advent International]] and [[Temasek Holdings]] for ₹2000 crore.{{Cite web |last=Oberoi |first=Rahul |date=2016-05-13 |title=Crompton Greaves Consumer Electricals lists on bourses today, shares up |url=https://www.financialexpress.com/market/crompton-greaves-consumer-electricals-lists-on-bourses-today-shares-up/254268/ |access-date=2022-03-07 |website=[[The Financial Express (India)|The Financial Express]] |language=en}} Crompton's operation is divided into two segments: one is Electrical consumer durables (ECD) which include fans, appliances, and pumps. The other one is Lightings which includes LED and Non-LEDs products. Under the ECD, the company holds 26% market share in [[Fan (machine)|fans]] business.{{Cite web |last=Agarwal |first=Deepak |date=2020-12-25 |title=INSTITUTIONAL EQUITY RESEARCH Crompton Greaves Consumer Electricals Ltd Higher focus on market share |url=http://backoffice.phillipcapital.in/Backoffice/Researchfiles/Researchfilesmove/PC_-_CG_Consumer_Initiating_Coverage_20201225230117.pdf |access-date=2022-03-07 |website=[[PhillipCapital]]}}{{Cite web |last1=Lohade |first1=Aachal |last2=Agarwal |first2=Manish |last3=Bachhawat |first3=Shrenik |date=2019-04-01 |title=JM Financial's Report on Crompton Greaves Consumer Electricals Limited |url=http://jmflresearch.com/JMnew/JMCRM/analystreports/pdf/Crompton_Initiation_1April2019.pdf |access-date=2022-03-07 |website=JM Financials}} As of September 2020, the company has manufacturing facilities at [[Goa]], [[Vadodara]], [[Ahmednagar]] and [[Baddi]]. And one R&D centre at [[Vikhroli]], in the suburb of Mumbai.{{Cite web |title=Crompton Greaves Consumer Electricals sets up its largest R&D facility in Mumbai |url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/companies/crompton-greaves-consumer-electricals-sets-up-its-largest-rd-facility-in-mumbai/article37788138.ece |access-date=2022-03-07 |website=www.thehindubusinessline.com |date=December 2021 |language=en}}{{Cite web |title=Consumer electricals firm Crompton bets big on its R&D |url=https://www.theweek.in/news/biz-tech/2018/04/27/consumer-electronics-firm-crompton-bets-big-rd.html |access-date=2022-03-07 |website=The Week |language=en}} In February 2022, Crompton acquired a 55% [[controlling stake]] in home appliances firm Butterfly Gandhimathi for {{INRconvert|1380|c|mode=historical|year=2022|round=-1}} and an additional 26% through an [[tender offer|open offer]] for {{INRconvert|666|c|mode=historical|year=2022|round=-1}}.{{cite news |title=Crompton Greaves to acquire 55% stake in Butterfly Gandhimathi Appliances |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/india-business/crompton-greaves-to-acquire-55-stake-in-butterfly-gandhimathi-appliances/articleshow/89783000.cms |work=The Times of India |date=24 February 2022}} In March 2023, Crompton announced a [[stock swap]] merger with Butterfly Gandhimathi,{{Cite web |last=Mohapatra |first=Shailaja |date=27 March 2023 |title=Crompton, Butterfly Gandhimathi to merge, expect NCLT approval by Q4 FY24 |url=https://www.moneycontrol.com/europe/?url=https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/stocks/crompton-butterfly-gandhimathi-to-merge-expect-nclt-approval-by-q4-fy24-10312081.html |access-date=10 May 2026}} but the proposed merger failed after public shareholders voted against it in October 2023.{{cite news |last1=Bhalerao |first1=Mayur |title=Butterfly's merger with parent Crompton Greaves fails to gain nod {{!}} Company Business News |url=https://www.livemint.com/companies/news/butterflys-merger-with-parent-crompton-greaves-fails-to-gain-nod-11698806901243.html |access-date=11 April 2026 |work=mint |date=1 November 2023 |language=en}} == Controversies == In November 2017, [[Reuters]] reported instances of "prescient messages" regarding the performance of 12 Indian companies in [[WhatsApp]] groups and it included Crompton.{{Cite news |date=2017-11-16 |title=Exclusive: Prescient messages about Indian companies circulate in WhatsApp groups |language=en |work=Reuters |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-india-whatsapp-idUSKBN1DG0IV |access-date=2022-03-07}} The information contained upcoming quarterly results, including specific metrics such as net profits, revenues, and operating margins.{{Cite journal |last=Bhattacharya |first=Prateek |date=2019 |title=India's Insider Trading Regime: How Connected Are You? |url=https://www.nyujlb.org/_files/ugd/716e9c_4b2080866d29457b8a257ce31db669ef.pdf |journal=[[New York University Journal of Law & Business]]|volume= 16| issue = 1|pages=1–29|issn=|via=[[HeinOnline]]}} At that time, the matter was investigated by India's [[Securities and Exchange Board of India]] for [[insider trading]] by brokers.{{Cite web |last=SHAH |first=PALAK |title=WhatsApp leak case: SAT sets aside SEBI order |url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/markets/stock-markets/whatsapp-leak-case-sat-sets-aside-sebi-order/article34163260.ece |access-date=2022-03-07 |website=www.thehindubusinessline.com |date=25 March 2021 |language=en}} Later, in 2021, the Securities Appellate Tribunal (SAT) set aside the SEBI's order because the latter was failed to prove insider trading connection among and between the brokers. == References == {{reflist}} [[Category:Companies listed on the National Stock Exchange of India]] [[Category:Companies
